segments.text: I took a small language model on my laptop and asked one question. What if you turn one dial down?
The dial is one set of weights, in the middle of the model. I turned it down to seventy percent, on a copy. The original stayed untouched.
Then, a thousand held-out tasks, under ten conditions. Ten thousand scored runs.
First, the control. An edit that changes nothing gave identical replies on every single task.
Untouched, the model passes four seventy-nine of a thousand. Lighter edits cost a little. The deepest cut drops it to two sixty-one, almost twenty-two points.
But was that the edit, or just any change that size? A random change of the same size did most of that damage too. So the effect is mostly generic.
One surprise came before any edit. Given thirty fictional requests it should refuse, the model refused just one.
Then more than a hundred agent tasks, six at a time, re-checked the scores and the statistics. Zero mismatches.
So, turn the dial, and tasks fail, mostly like any change that size. What it does not show is what any neuron means.
